findings.problem: The health-check options map passes `wiki: data.xwikiWiki` unguarded, while the create path 200 lines below deliberately collapses the same value with `values.xwikiWiki || undefined`. dataSourceStore.healthCheckDatasource spreads on `options.wiki != null`, and '' != null is true, so a blank Wiki field is sent to v1/index/health as `"wiki": ""`.
findings.impact: Leaving Wiki blank is the documented default path (the backend defaults it to 'xwiki'). An explicit empty string overrides that default, so the pre-create health check probes wiki '' instead of 'xwiki' — a false negative that blocks creation with a confusing error. Verified: DatasourceHealthCheckRequest.wiki has no minLength, so this does not 422, but it does defeat the default.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the create path: `[INDEX_TYPES.XWIKI]: { space: data.xwikiSpace, wiki: data.xwikiWiki || undefined }`.

findings.problem: On a failed health check the form calls `setError(response.error.field_error, ...)` with the backend's field name. Verified in the sibling backend at service/index/datasource_health_check_service.py:309-310: DatasourceTypes.XWIKI maps to the field name "space". The form registers that input as `xwikiSpace`, so setError targets a field that does not exist and no input is flagged.
findings.impact: When the backend rejects the space (bad space key, too many pages), the user sees only the generic health-check banner with no indication that Space is the field to fix. This is a regression relative to Confluence, whose backend field_error 'cql' matches its form field name exactly — it is the direct cost of the xwikiSpace/xwikiWiki prefixing decision.
findings.recommendation: Add a small backend-field → form-field map before the setError call (space → xwikiSpace, wiki → xwikiWiki) with a passthrough default, and ignore names that are not form fields. Do not revert the prefixed naming.

findings.problem: `wiki: values.xwikiWiki || undefined` is correct for create but wrong for the edit path, which reuses the same request object. Verified in the sibling backend at rest_api/models/index.py:776-789: `_update_xwiki_fields` applies `if wiki is not None`, so an omitted wiki means 'keep the stored value' on PUT.
findings.impact: Edit a datasource stored as `xwiki: { space: 'KB', wiki: 'teamwiki' }`, clear the Wiki field, save. The request omits wiki, the backend keeps 'teamwiki', and the save reports success — but the datasource keeps indexing teamwiki. Reopening the edit form repopulates 'teamwiki' with no error. The UI and the stored state silently disagree.
findings.recommendation: Branch the collapse on mode: keep `|| undefined` for create, and on update send the user's explicit intent — `wiki: values.xwikiWiki || 'xwiki'` — which satisfies the PUT schema's minLength-1 and actually reverts to the default.

findings.problem: Two non-obvious behaviours introduced by this change have no coverage: the empty-wiki-to-omitted-key collapse, and the entire xWiki edit/update path (including the `defaults?.xwiki?.space / .wiki` prefill). The POST-body test always fills Wiki in; the scheduling test leaves it blank but asserts only on cron_expression.
findings.impact: Changing `wiki: values.xwikiWiki || undefined` to `wiki: values.xwikiWiki` leaves the suite green while every real create with a blank Wiki sends an empty string (CR-001's failure mode, and a 422 against the create schema's minLength-1). The edit branch and prefill can break entirely without any test failing.
findings.recommendation: Assert `expect(body).not.toHaveProperty('wiki')` in the blank-Wiki case, and add an edit-mode test that renders with an index carrying `xwiki: { space, wiki }`, asserts the prefill, and asserts the PUT body.

rationale: All three lenses ran against a fully readable 951-line diff with the approved spec present, so coverage is complete and confidence is high. Four major findings survived triage, all bucketed `patch` (mechanical fixes, no open design questions), which is why the decision is request-changes rather than an escalation. Three of the four cluster on one root cause: the optional `wiki` field is handled inconsistently across the three request paths it feeds (health check sends '', create omits, update omits-and-therefore-cannot-clear). CR-002 is the one genuinely new cost of the xwikiSpace/xwikiWiki naming decision — the backend's field_error contract assumes the form field is named after the API field, which holds for Confluence but not here; the fix is a small mapping, not a naming reversal. Two claims resting on the unmerged sibling backend were independently verified against ../codemie source rather than taken on trust: the XWIKI→"space" field_error mapping and the `if wiki is not None` update semantics. 1 finding dismissed: the blind lens flagged the NEW-badge assertion as potentially vacuous, but this was empirically refuted — reverting only the XWIKI badge clause makes that test fail, so it is correctly scoped. 0 deferred. Standards are clean: all 8 commit subjects match the documented format, lint/typecheck/license-headers/gitleaks all pass. Note that the full unit suite has 6 pre-existing failures in 4 locale-dependent files (analyticsFormatters, SkillInstructions, ReleaseNotesPage, WorkflowExecutionInfoPopup); these were confirmed to fail identically on main and are unrelated to this change. Live end-to-end verification against the running stack has not yet run — that is Stage 7.
